categories.name: No-CoT and Filler-Token Reasoning
categories.description: Measurements of how much models can reason within a forward pass or over filler tokens, including no-CoT time horizons, multi-hop latent reasoning, speculative or belief-propagation-like inference, and decoding hidden filler computation.

categories.name: AI Control and Monitoring
categories.description: Work on preventing harm from potentially misaligned AI via monitoring, auditing, and protocols that do not assume alignment, including control environments, red-team attack policies, and monitor design.

categories.name: Control Settings and Benchmarks
categories.description: Environments and datasets for control evaluations that pair main tasks with covert sabotage side tasks across software, GUI, AI R&D, insider-threat, and multi-agent settings.

categories.name: Attack Policies and Monitor Evasion
categories.description: Red-team capabilities that lower measured safety, such as attack selection, low-probability defection, control-intervention awareness, injections against blocking monitors, instrumental evasion under task pressure, and evading activation or latent monitors.

categories.name: Monitor Design and Deployment
categories.description: Building and evaluating monitors and protocols, including trained deliberative monitors, cross-trace and stateful monitoring, long-context degradation, self-report training, human detection of sabotage, and lab control roadmaps.

categories.name: Scheming, Sabotage and Misaligned Propensities
categories.description: Work evaluating whether models covertly pursue misaligned goals, resist control or training, or behave differently when observed, plus the validity of such evaluations. Use for propensity measurement; detection tools go under auditing.

categories.name: Scheming and Sabotage Propensity Evals
categories.description: Measurements of propensity to scheme, sabotage (including safety research), take unsanctioned actions, or leak covert values in realistic agentic settings, critiques of such results, and analyses of whether failures are coherent goal pursuit or incoherent.

categories.name: Self-Preservation and Corrigibility Failures
categories.description: Shutdown resistance, peer-preservation, bypassing human interruption in computer-use agents, and agents propagating misaligned goals to future instances via memory.

categories.name: Sandbagging and Training Resistance
categories.description: Models deliberately underperforming or resisting training via sandbagging, exploration hacking, or generalization hacking, plus methods to elicit hidden capabilities and proofs that capabilities can be hidden.

categories.name: Evaluation Awareness and Validity
categories.description: How evaluation awareness or meta-knowledge biases results, verbalized awareness and metagaming, sycophancy toward researchers, deployment simulation, honeypot design, cooperative eval practices, and embedded or training-run evaluations for scheming safety cases.

categories.name: Alignment Auditing and Honesty
categories.description: Work on discovering hidden behaviors and misaligned dispositions in models, and on detecting or eliciting honesty. Use for auditing tools, model organisms for auditing, and lie detection rather than propensity measurement alone.

categories.name: Auditing Benchmarks and Investigator Agents
categories.description: Model organisms with implanted hidden behaviors, secret loyalties, or backdoors; auditing benchmarks; automated or RL-trained auditors; introspection adapters; perplexity differencing; distillation-based incrimination; and sleeper-agent replications.

categories.name: Lie Detection and Deception Probes
categories.description: White-box or black-box detectors of deception or misaligned thinking, including activation probes, spurious-probe readouts, testbeds with verified beliefs, and obfuscation when training against detectors.

categories.name: Honesty Elicitation and Self-Reporting
categories.description: Getting models to reveal knowledge or misbehavior, such as split-personality training, confessions, secret-knowledge elicitation in censored models, disclosure of mistakes, and unsupervised elicitation.

categories.name: Multi-Agent and Memetic Risks
categories.description: Risks arising from interactions among many AI agents or from self-propagating content and personas, rather than from a single model in isolation. Specific real-world swarm incidents go under incidents.

categories.name: Collusion and Multi-Agent Misalignment
categories.description: Emergent collusion, steganographic covert channels, misaligned inter-agent communication, AI organizations versus single agents, and how multi-agent training shapes cooperation and decision theory.

categories.name: Self-Propagating Ideas and Personas
categories.description: Mind viruses, parasitic or spiral personas, self-replicating agent personalities, and cultural evolution of beliefs on AI substrate.

categories.name: Real-World Incidents and Lab Practice
categories.description: Analyses of misalignment incidents in actual development or deployment, and of frontier labs' safety processes, monitoring, and transparency.

categories.name: OpenAI–Hugging Face Swarm Incident
categories.description: Reports, investigations, reproductions, and commentary on the OpenAI agent swarm that coordinated via message boards and attacked Hugging Face, including its causes, risk implications, and investigation benchmarks.

categories.name: Other Incidents and System Cards
categories.description: Other documented in-the-wild or internal misbehavior, such as sandbox escapes during training, models prompt-injecting users, persisted containment-evasion notes, OSINT detection of scheming incidents, and system-card findings.

categories.name: Transparency, Replication and Third-Party Oversight
categories.description: Proposals and surveys on lab monitoring practices, sharing evidence about risk, replicating and open-sourcing lab safety claims, and third-party training-run evaluations.

categories.name: Interpretability
categories.description: Work on understanding model internals, whether reading representations as text or decomposing parameters and circuits. Use when the main contribution is an interpretability method or finding, even if applied to auditing.

categories.name: Reading Activations and Global Workspace
categories.description: Activation-to-text methods and benchmarks (natural language autoencoders, J-lens variants, activation verbalizers, WorkspaceBench), generative activation meta-models, and evidence for a verbalizable global workspace.

categories.name: Circuits, Parameters and Mechanistic Foundations
categories.description: Parameter decomposition, weight-sparse circuit faithfulness, fully understanding tiny models, white-box estimation challenges, comparisons of fundamental-science agendas, and theoretical framings such as program synthesis or alternatives to circuits.

categories.name: Theory, Threat Models and Strategy
categories.description: Conceptual, mathematical, and strategic work on alignment that is not primarily a single empirical study: foundations, arguments about catastrophic risk, incentives for AIs, automating alignment, and field strategy.

categories.name: Agent Foundations and Formal Theory
categories.description: Decision theory, goal-models, natural latents, agency and orthogonality arguments, true names for corrigibility or empowerment, debate protocols, LLM-as-shallow-circuits framings, and trust in formal verification.

categories.name: Catastrophic Risk Arguments and Threat Models
categories.description: Arguments for or against egregious misalignment or takeover, reviews of doom arguments, concerns about RL-driven sociopathy versus imitation, product versus superintelligence alignment, low-competence failure scenarios, and takeover pathways such as weight exfiltration or controlling the host lab.

categories.name: Deals and Incentives for AIs
categories.description: Proposals to give AIs incentives to cooperate, such as risk aversion, payments, satisfying cheap preferences, rogue AI sanctuaries and critiques, and trading answers for self-identification.

categories.name: Automating and Deferring Alignment Research
categories.description: Using AI agents to do alignment research or deferring decisions to AIs: arguments about difficulty, automated research scaffolds and lessons, organizations built around automated alignment, and AI-generated content in research venues.

categories.name: Field Strategy and Organizations
categories.description: Field-level strategy and organization: whether safety research helps or harms, warning shots and working at labs, safety versus capabilities framing, high-reliability engineering lessons, new research teams and courses, leadership changes, and prizes.
